title: First Sea Fishing — National Day on the Coast
excerpt: Blue mackerel scad, rabbitfish, and a seaside sunset during my first deep-sea fishing trip.
body: During the National Day holiday I tried sea fishing for the first time. Luck was on my side — blue mackerel scad and rabbitfish, plus a sunset that made the wait worthwhile.
There's a different rhythm to research life when you step away from the bench: salt air, long silences, and small victories measured in centimeters of line rather than nanometers of interface.
My bait setup kept getting stolen by smaller fish. A seasoned fisherman nearby noticed and offered a tip: "They can feel the weight of your hook. Go lighter."
Adapt or go home with empty hands. Sound familiar?
Changed the rig, kept the patience, and eventually landed three decent catches.
• The water changes color with depth — turquoise near shore, dark navy beyond
• Patience is a skill; I need more practice
